svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "pH curves for titrations with 0.100 mol dm\u207b\u00b3 sodium hydroxide."], [1, "Strong acid: pH starts at 1 and jumps steeply at equivalence, pH 7."], [5.5, "Weak acid (ethanoic acid): higher start, a buffer region, equivalence above pH 7."], [10, "At half-equivalence, pH = pKa = 4.76."], [12.5, "Choose an indicator whose range lies on the steep part."]]
svg.title: Acid–base titration curves
svg.desc: pH curves for titrating 25.0 cm3 of 0.100 mol dm-3 hydrochloric acid and ethanoic acid with 0.100 mol dm-3 sodium hydroxide, showing equivalence points, the half-equivalence point where pH equals pKa, and indicator ranges.
svg.text: 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ acid; 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH added. Curves calculated.

g.data-info: 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ HCl with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH: starts at pH 1, rises slowly, then a long vertical section (about pH 3–11) at equivalence (25.0 cm³), pH 7.
Ethanoic acid (pKa 4.76): starts near pH 2.9, a gently rising buffer region, equivalence at pH about 8.7 (ethanoate ions are basic); shorter steep section, about pH 7–11.
Before equivalence the mixture of ethanoic acid and ethanoate resists changes in pH.
Moles of base added = moles of acid at the start (25.0 cm³ here).
At 12.5 cm³, half the acid is neutralised: [HA] = [A⁻], so pH = pKa = 4.76. A way to find pKa.
Its colour change range must fall within the steep section: phenolphthalein (8.3–10.0) works for both curves here; methyl orange (3.1–4.4) only for the strong acid.

g.text: buffer region; pH = pKa at 12.5 cm³
range must lie in the steep part:
methyl orange only the strong acid
